sentence.ja: 六時[ろくじ]に{家[いえ]}に帰[かえ]ります。
sentence.en: I go home at six.

mnemonic.story: Every time you come back to your **house**, the old front door creaks a long "*ee-yeh*". Ie: the house, the building itself. One more i makes iie, "no".

sentence.ja: 週末[しゅうまつ]、{うち}へ来[き]ませんか。
sentence.en: Do you want to come over to my place this weekend?

mnemonic.story: You walk into **my place** and smell toast with melted cheese: "*Ooh, cheese!*" Uchi is home as in where your people are; ie is the building.

sentence.ja: 私[わたし]の{部屋[へや]}に猫[ねこ]がいます。
sentence.en: There's a cat in my room.

mnemonic.story: You kick open the door of your **room** with a karate "*Hey-yah!*" and a tower of laundry topples onto the floor. Heya: room.

sentence.ja: あれはトイレの{ドア}ですよ。
sentence.en: That over there is the restroom door.

mnemonic.story: *Door* becomes do-a, two short beats, the r opening out into an ah. **Door**.

sentence.ja: {窓[まど]}の近[ちか]くに猫[ねこ]がいます。
sentence.en: There's a cat near the window.

mnemonic.story: *Ma* slaps a lump of bread *dough* against the kitchen **window** to cool it, and it slides slowly down the glass, leaving a floury smear. Mado: window.

sentence.ja: 先生[せんせい]の{机[つくえ]}はあそこです。
sentence.en: The teacher's desk is over there.

mnemonic.story: You slap your new **desk**, the polished wood humming under your palm: "*It's cool, eh?*" Clip it down to ts-ku-e and you have the word. Tsukue: desk.

sentence.ja: 机[つくえ]の前[まえ]に{いす}があります。
sentence.en: There's a chair in front of the desk.

mnemonic.story: You drop onto an old **chair** and it squeals "*eee*", then the cushion sighs "*sss*" as the air leaks out. Isu: chair.

sentence.ja: 昨日[きのう]の夜[よる]は{電気[でんき]}がありませんでした。
sentence.en: We had no electricity last night.

mnemonic.story: You turn a brass *key* in the wall of your *den* and **electricity** crackles into every bulb, the whole room humming. Den-ki: electricity; also the light itself.

sentence.ja: 暑[あつ]いですから、{エアコン}をつけてもいいですか。
sentence.en: It's hot, so may I turn on the air conditioner?

breakdown.en: it's all right to turn on

mnemonic.story: *Air conditioner* shrinks to two short pieces: e-a for air, kon from the front of conditioner. E-a-kon, the **air conditioner**.

sentence.ja: ホテルの{お風呂[ふろ]}はとても大[おお]きかったです。
sentence.en: The bath at the hotel was really big.

mnemonic.story: Polite o plus *furrow*: you soak so long in the hot **bath** that your fingertips wrinkle into deep furrows and steam fogs the mirror. O-furo: bath.

sentence.ja: ホテルの{シャワー}はとても熱[あつ]かったです。
sentence.en: The shower at the hotel was really hot.

mnemonic.story: *Shower* becomes sha-wā: the -er at the end melts into a long ā. **Shower**.

sentence.ja: すみません、{お手洗[てあら]い}はどこですか。
sentence.en: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

mnemonic.story: Polite o, *te* for hand, *arai* for washing: the honourable hand-washing place, a politer word for the **restroom** than toire. O-te-arai: restroom.

sentence.ja: この{パソコン}を使[つか]ってもいいですか。
sentence.en: May I use this computer?

mnemonic.story: *Personal computer* is clipped to the front of each word: pa-so from pāsonaru, kon from konpyūtā. Paso-kon, a **personal computer**.

sentence.ja: 暑[あつ]いから、窓[まど]を{開[あ]けました}。
sentence.en: It was hot, so I opened the window.

mnemonic.story: You pry **open** *a keg* and foam bursts out with a hiss, soaking your sleeves and smelling of hops. Ake-ru: to open something.

sentence.ja: 寒[さむ]いですから、ドアを{閉[し]めて}ください。
sentence.en: It's cold, so please close the door.

mnemonic.story: The doorway starts to *shimmer* like heat haze, and you slam it **closed** before whatever is shimmering can step through. Shime-ru: to close, the opposite of ake-ru.

sentence.ja: 部屋[へや]のエアコンを{つけて}ください。
sentence.en: Please turn on the air conditioner in the room.

mnemonic.story: You *sketch* a light switch on the wall in chalk, press it, and the lamp clicks **on**. The kestrel's word, kes-u, turns it back off. Tsuke-ru: to turn on.

sentence.ja: ここにごみを{捨[す]てないで}ください。
sentence.en: Please don't throw trash away here.

mnemonic.story: The bread is *stale*, hard as a brick, so you **throw away** the whole loaf and it lands in the bin with a thud. Sute-ru: to throw away.

sentence.ja: 友達[ともだち]に自転車[じてんしゃ]を{借[か]りました}。
sentence.en: I borrowed a bike from a friend.

mnemonic.story: You **borrow** a pot of *curry* from your neighbour and carry it home across the hall, steam fogging your glasses. Kari-ru: to borrow; kaes-u gives it back.

sentence.ja: 部屋[へや]の電気[でんき]を{消[け]して}ください。
sentence.en: Please turn off the light in the room.

mnemonic.story: A *kestrel* swoops into your bedroom, pecks the switch, and the lamp clicks **off**; then it flaps across the whiteboard and wipes it clean. Kes-u: to turn off; also to erase.

sentence.ja: このペンを{使[つか]って}もいいですか。
sentence.en: May I use this pen?

mnemonic.story: You **use** *two cows* as a lawnmower, and their teeth tear across the grass with a steady crunch while you sip lemonade. Tsuka-u: to use.

sentence.ja: 手[て]を{洗[あら]って}ください。
sentence.en: Please wash your hands.

mnemonic.story: Mud swirls down the drain as you scrub *a raw* potato under the cold tap, because anything raw you always **wash** first. Ara-u: to wash.

sentence.ja: どうぞ、ここに{座[すわ]って}ください。
sentence.en: Please, have a seat here.

mnemonic.story: You go to **sit down** on a park bench, but a *swan* is already on it, hissing and flapping, refusing to budge an inch. Suwa-ru: to sit down.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さん、ちょっと{立[た]って}ください。
sentence.en: Tanaka-san, could you stand up for a moment?

mnemonic.story: You **stand up** on your chair to show off a fresh *tattoo* across your calf, and the whole café stands up with you to get a look. Ta-tsu: to stand up.

sentence.ja: 週末[しゅうまつ]、母[はは]の料理[りょうり]を{手伝[てつだ]います}。
sentence.en: On weekends I help my mother with the cooking.

mnemonic.story: "*Ted's down!*" someone shouts, and you rush to **help** haul your friend out of a snowdrift, his boots kicking and snow down your sleeves. Tetsuda-u: to help.

sentence.ja: 山田[やまだ]さんに傘[かさ]を{返[かえ]して}ください。
sentence.en: Please give the umbrella back to Yamada-san.

mnemonic.story: Before you **return** your friend's borrowed guitar, you give its strings one long *caress*, a last soft strum, then hand it back. Kaes-u: to return a thing to someone.

sentence.ja: 部屋[へや]を{掃除[そうじ]して}ください。
sentence.en: Please clean your room.

mnemonic.story: You open your brother's bedroom door and gasp, "*So... jeez!*", then spend all Saturday **cleaning** it, the mop squelching across sticky floorboards. Sōji suru: to clean.

sentence.ja: 週末[しゅうまつ]に服[ふく]を{洗濯[せんたく]します}。
sentence.en: I wash my clothes on the weekend.

mnemonic.story: The laundromat machine takes one *cent* and one *taco*, so you **do the laundry** and pull out warm shirts that smell faintly of salsa. Sentaku suru: to do laundry.

sentence.ja: {頭[あたま]}が痛[いた]いです。
sentence.en: I have a headache.

mnemonic.story: You bonk your **head** on a shelf, see *atoms* spinning round it like cartoon stars, and yell "*Ma!*" A-ta-ma: head.

sentence.ja: 毎朝[まいあさ]、{顔[かお]}を洗[あら]います。
sentence.en: I wash my face every morning.

mnemonic.story: A *cow* pushes its big wet **face** through your kitchen window and licks your cheek with a rough, warm tongue. Ka-o: face.

sentence.ja: 妹[いもうと]は{髪[かみ]}が長[なが]くてきれいです。
sentence.en: My younger sister's hair is long and pretty.

mnemonic.story: After a windy ferry ride your **hair** sticks straight up and seems to beg "*calm me*", so you press it down with both damp palms. Kami: hair.

sentence.ja: 姉[あね]は{目[め]}がきれいです。
sentence.en: My older sister has beautiful eyes.

mnemonic.story: A bored goat stares you down with one yellow **eye** and bleats a flat *meh*, chewing all the while. Me: eye.

sentence.ja: うちの猫[ねこ]は{耳[みみ]}が大[おお]きいです。
sentence.en: Our cat has big ears.

mnemonic.story: The choir member beside you sings warm-up scales straight into your **ear**, *mi, mi, mi*, until it rings. Mimi: ear.

sentence.ja: 犬[いぬ]は{鼻[はな]}がいいです。
sentence.en: Dogs have a good nose.

mnemonic.soundsLike: ha... nah (a sneeze that won't come)
mnemonic.story: You bury your **nose** in a flower, and it tickles: *ha... nah*, the sneeze that never arrives. Nose and flower share the sound hana. Hana: nose.

sentence.ja: ケンさんは{口[くち]}が大[おお]きいです。
sentence.en: Ken has a wide mouth.

mnemonic.story: At the picnic you open your **mouth** wide, and a friend lobs a cube of *cool cheese* straight in from three metres away. Kuchi: mouth.

sentence.ja: 毎晩[まいばん]{歯[は]}を磨[みが]きます。
sentence.en: I brush my teeth every night.

mnemonic.story: One short *ha!* and your gold **tooth** flashes in the sun. One ha is a tooth; haha, two of them, is your mother. Ha: tooth.

sentence.ja: カラオケで歌[うた]いすぎて、{のど}が痛[いた]いです。
sentence.en: I sang too much at karaoke, and my throat hurts.

mnemonic.story: A lump of raw pizza *dough* lodges in your **throat**. '*No dough*!' you croak, swearing off it forever as it slides down, cold and gummy. Nodo: throat.

sentence.ja: キリンは{首[くび]}が長[なが]いです。
sentence.en: Giraffes have long necks.

mnemonic.story: A *cool bee* in tiny sunglasses lands on the back of your **neck** and crawls under your collar, buzzing. Kubi: neck.

sentence.ja: 猫[ねこ]が私[わたし]の{肩[かた]}に乗[の]っています。
sentence.en: The cat is sitting on my shoulder.

mnemonic.story: Halfway through a karate *kata*, your partner's chop lands on your **shoulder**, thwack, and it aches all week. Kata: shoulder.

sentence.ja: {手[て]}を上[あ]げてください。
sentence.en: Please raise your hand.

mnemonic.story: You hold up both **hands** and count *ten* fingers out loud, then the n falls off the end like a dropped ring. Te: hand.

sentence.ja: 赤[あか]ちゃんが私[わたし]の{指[ゆび]}を持[も]っています。
sentence.en: The baby is holding my finger.

mnemonic.story: A bee lands on your **finger** and stings it, and you shake the swelling finger at it: "*You, bee!*" Yubi: finger.

sentence.ja: さくらさんは{足[あし]}が長[なが]いです。
sentence.en: Sakura has long legs.

mnemonic.story: You wade barefoot through a cold fireplace, and your **legs** come out grey and *ashy* right up to the knee. Ashi: leg; foot.

sentence.ja: {おなか}がすきました。
sentence.en: I'm hungry.

mnemonic.story: O is polite and naka is middle: your **stomach** is your honourable middle. When it's empty it rumbles like someone at a door: *oh, knock-a, knock-a*. O-naka: stomach.

sentence.ja: {背中[せなか]}がかゆいです。
sentence.en: My back is itchy.

mnemonic.story: Se is the back, the height you *say* things up to in se ga takai, and naka is middle. Senaka is the middle of your **back**, where an itch always lands out of reach. Se-naka: back.

sentence.ja: 先週[せんしゅう]は{病気[びょうき]}でした。
sentence.en: I was sick last week.

mnemonic.story: Flat in bed with an **illness**, you keep croaking *be okey*, *be okey* through a stuffed nose that squashes okay into okey, the thermometer beeping. Byōki: illness.

sentence.ja: {風邪[かぜ]}なので、早[はや]く寝[ね]ます。
sentence.en: I have a cold, so I'm going to bed early.

breakdown.baseEn: to sleep, to go to bed

mnemonic.story: Your **cold** has turned your nose into a *kazoo*: every sniffle buzzes, every blow honks, and wet tissues pile up around you. Kaze: a cold (wind is also kaze).

sentence.ja: {せき}が止[と]まらないんです。
sentence.en: My cough won't stop.

mnemonic.story: One violent **cough** and you hack up a whole *set* of *keys* on a ring, jangling across the table. Seki: cough.

sentence.ja: 病院[びょういん]で{薬[くすり]}をもらいました。
sentence.en: I got some medicine at the hospital.

mnemonic.story: A sick pigeon goes *coo*; you mutter *sorry* as you push a bitter **medicine** tablet into its beak, and it shudders every feather. Kusuri: medicine.

sentence.ja: 頭[あたま]が{痛[いた]い}んです。
sentence.en: I have a headache.

mnemonic.story: Dared by friends, you *eat a* whole cactus, and every spine **hurts** on the way down. Ita-i: painful; yelped on its own, itai! means ouch.

sentence.ja: 雨[あめ]の中[なか]を歩[ある]いて、{風邪[かぜ]をひきました}。
sentence.en: I walked in the rain and caught a cold.

mnemonic.story: Hiku means to pull: you **catch a cold** by pulling it in, like reeling a soggy *kazoo* out of an icy lake, *hiccup*ping with every tug. Kaze o hiku: to catch a cold.

sentence.ja: {熱[ねつ]がある}ので、病院[びょういん]へ行[い]きます。
sentence.en: I have a fever, so I'm going to the hospital.

mnemonic.story: You lie tangled in hot fishing *nets*, sweating, too weak to throw them off: you **have a fever**. Netsu is the fever, ga aru says you have one. Netsu ga aru.

sentence.ja: まだ{薬[くすり]を飲[の]んでいません}。
sentence.en: I haven't taken my medicine yet.

mnemonic.story: Japanese drinks medicine instead of taking it: kusuri o *nomu*, even for a dry pill. You toss the tablet back and wash it down, glug. Kusuri o nomu: **to take medicine**.

sentence.ja: ケンさんは{背[せ]が高[たか]い}です。
sentence.en: Ken is tall.

mnemonic.story: Your friend is so **tall** that you *say* everything upward, chin tilted to the ceiling. Se is height and takai is high: "the height is high". Se ga taka-i: tall.

sentence.ja: 妹[いもうと]は{背[せ]が低[ひく]い}です。
sentence.en: My younger sister is short.

mnemonic.story: Your **short** cousin gets the *hiccups*, and with every hic he seems to sink lower. Se ga hikui, "the height is low"; use it for people, not mijikai. Se ga hiku-i: short.

sentence.ja: たくさん歩[ある]いたから、{疲[つか]れました}。
sentence.en: I walked a lot, so I'm tired.

mnemonic.story: You push *two cars* up a hill, one after the other, and by the top you **get tired**: legs shaking, shirt soaked. Tsukare-ru: to get tired.

sentence.ja: {心配[しんぱい]しない}でください。
sentence.en: Please don't worry.

breakdown.text: 心配しないでください

mnemonic.story: You **worry** so much about the oven that you pace the kitchen, crack your *shin* on the door, and the *pie* burns anyway. Shinpai suru: to worry.

sentence.ja: {たぶん}明日[あした]は雨[あめ]だと思[おも]います。
sentence.en: I think it'll probably rain tomorrow.

mnemonic.story: Is it *taboo* to eat the last dumpling? **Probably**, you decide, chewing it slowly anyway while the whole table glares. Tabun: probably, maybe.

sentence.ja: {できるだけ}野菜[やさい]を食[た]べたほうがいいですよ。
sentence.en: You should eat as many vegetables as you can.

breakdown.text: 食べたほうがいいです

mnemonic.story: Dekiru is 'can do', dake is 'only': only up to what you can. You pile your *deck* chair with books **as much as possible**, until it creaks and folds flat. Dekiru dake.
